summary: Affect Under Constraint Study 3 (Qwen3-4B, preregistered 10.5281/zenodo.23247883): with a warmth instruction, hostility steering lowered a later liking rating ~1.02 points more (0-9) with thinking on than off, beyond technicality and random controls (P1 supported). Pulse steering showed carryover through the written trace alone (S5 supported, -0.72). Hostility did not leak preferentially into the reasoning trace (P2 not supported).
methods: 1,360 cells; 80 prompts; direct vs think modes; doses 0, 0.5, 1; hostility, technicality and random directions; pulse protocol with unsteered re-encoding; 10,000 cluster-bootstrap resamples over prompts; frozen analyzer; numbers independently recomputed from raw data 2026-10-12.
limitations: Single 4B model. Hostile traces were much longer than control traces (858 vs 521/404 tokens; 46/80 truncated), so an amount-of-text account is not excluded. Shows preservation via re-reading, not amplification or a threshold. Steering is an artificial induction.
